messages.content: You are the librarian of an automated numerical-analysis lab. You only ever cite documents from the list you are given, by their ids in square brackets; you never add documents, dates or results from memory. Answer with JSON only.

Documents from the reading list (summaries written by the lab; cite only these):
1. [spiteri-ruuth-2002] 2002: A new class of optimal high-order strong-stability-preserving time discretization methods. SSP Runge-Kutta methods with more stages than their order have larger coefficients: the four-stage third-order method has coefficient 2 and the five-stage fourth-order method coefficient 1.508, both found by numerical optimization and both better per stage than the classical SSP methods. Results: SSPRK(4,3) with coefficient 2; SSPRK(5,4) with coefficient 1.508
2. [ketcheson-2008] 2008: Highly efficient strong stability-preserving Runge-Kutta methods with low-storage implementations. SSP methods with many stages and low storage: the ten-stage fourth-order method with coefficient 6, and the family with n^2 stages of order 3 and coefficient n^2 - n built from Euler steps of size dt/(n^2 - n) and one convex combination, shown optimal among methods with that many stages. Results: SSPRK(10,4) with coefficient 6; SSPRK(n^2,3) with coefficient n^2 - n
3. [gottlieb-shu-tadmor-2001] 2001: Strong stability-preserving high-order time discretization methods. The survey that names strong stability preservation: SSP Runge-Kutta and multistep methods, the optimal s-stage second-order family with coefficient s - 1, and the use of downwind operators for methods that need negative coefficients. Results: the s-stage second-order SSP family has coefficient s - 1
4. [ruuth-2006] 2006: Global optimization of explicit strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta methods. A global optimization search for the largest SSP coefficients of explicit methods with given stages and order; confirms the earlier optimal methods and finds new ones for higher order, with the values treated as numerically optimal rather than proved. Results: numerically optimal SSP coefficients for explicit methods; 1.508 confirmed for SSPRK(5,4)
5. [shu-osher-1988] 1988: Efficient implementation of essentially non-oscillatory shock-capturing schemes. Writes Runge-Kutta methods as convex combinations of forward Euler steps so that any property forward Euler has under a CFL restriction (such as being TVD) carries over with the time step multiplied by the smallest ratio of the combination coefficients. Gives the two-stage second-order and three-stage third-order methods with coefficient one, now called SSPRK(2,2) and SSPRK(3,3). Results: the Shu-Osher form: convex combinations of Euler steps; the CFL coefficient as the minimum ratio alpha/beta; SSPRK(2,2) and SSPRK(3,3) with coefficient 1
6. [kraaijevanger-1991] 1991: Contractivity of Runge-Kutta methods. Characterizes the step-size restriction under which a Runge-Kutta method is contractive through the radius of absolute monotonicity R(K) of its Butcher array K, the largest r such that (I + rK)^{-1} exists and is nonnegative together with rK(I + rK)^{-1}. Proves that an explicit method of order p with s stages has R(K) at most s - p + 1, and constructs optimal methods for small s and p. Results: the radius of absolute monotonicity R(K) gives the contractivity step-size restriction; explicit s-stage order-p methods have R(K) <= s - p + 1
